question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form. Select the resulting augmented matrix.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(-1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ -1 & 2 & -1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_3:=R_3+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -1 & 0 & -3 \\ 0 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]
$$

metadata.domain: x,y,z real; p,q,s nonzero; nonsingular 3-by-3 coefficient matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M$ for the variables $x,y,z$ in that order.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ -1 & -2 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 0\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=0 \\ y &=1-(0)(0) \\ &=1 \\ x &=2-(2)(1) \\ &\quad -(-1)(0) \\ &=0\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(0,1,0\right)
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the system of linear equations

$$
\left\{\begin{aligned}x+2y &=-1 \\ -x-2y+z &=4 \\ y &=1\end{aligned}\right.
$$

Use the standard method of Gaussian elimination to reduce the augmented matrix to row echelon form, and then solve the linear system. Select the solution $(x,y,z)$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
The augmented matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ -1 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

$R_2:=R_2+(1)R_1$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

The second pivot is zero, while the third row has a nonzero second entry. Exchange $R_2$ and $R_3$.

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Thus the row echelon matrix is

$$
\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 2 & 0 & -1 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 1 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

Back substitute, starting with the last row:

$$
\begin{aligned}z &=3 \\ y &=1-(0)(3) \\ &=1 \\ x &=-1-(2)(1) \\ &\quad -(0)(3) \\ &=-3\end{aligned}
$$

The solution $(x,y,z)$ is

$$
\left(-3,1,3\right)
$$
